title: LRU Cache
topic: Design / Hash Table / Doubly Linked List
timeComplexity: O(1) for both get and put
oneLinerQuestion: Design a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache supporting get and put in O(1) time.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The LRU (Least Recently Used) Cache design problem requires implementing a fixed-capacity key-value cache supporting get(key) and put(key, value) operations in O(1) average time complexity, evicting the least recently accessed item when capacity is exceeded. While a Hash Map provides O(1) lookups, it cannot track recency order in O(1) time. Conversely, an array or singly linked list can order elements but requires O(N) shifts or scans to relocate accessed items. Pairing a Hash Map with a Doubly Linked List (DLL) achieves strict O(1) performance: the map associates keys with direct node pointers, and the bidirectional pointers of the DLL enable O(1) node detachment and re-insertion at the Most Recently Used (MRU) head, along with O(1) eviction from the Least Recently Used (LRU) tail.

- Step 1: Data Structure Blueprint & Node Definition — We define a doubly linked list node class containing `key`, `value`, `prev`, and `next` pointers. Storing the `key` inside each node is essential so that when an LRU node is evicted from the tail, we can immediately remove its corresponding entry from the Hash Map in O(1) time.

- Step 2: Cache Initialization & Dummy Sentinels — We initialize `capacity`, an empty Hash Map `cache = new Map()`, and two dummy sentinel nodes: `left` (LRU boundary) and `right` (MRU boundary). We link them together (`left.next = right` and `right.prev = left`), which eliminates edge cases when inserting into an empty list or deleting terminal nodes.

- Step 3: Helper Routines (Remove & Insert) — We implement two pointer helpers: `remove(node)` splices `node` out by updating `node.prev.next = node.next` and `node.next.prev = node.prev`. `insert(node)` places `node` immediately before `right` (the MRU position) by adjusting links between `right.prev`, `node`, and `right`.

- Step 4: Implementing get(key) — If `key` is not present in `cache`, return `-1`. Otherwise, retrieve the node via `const node = cache.get(key)`, mark it as recently accessed by calling `remove(node)` followed by `insert(node)`, and return `node.value`.

- Step 5: Implementing put(key, value) — If `key` already exists, retrieve the existing node, update its value (`node.value = value`), and call `remove(node)` followed by `insert(node)` to refresh its recency. If the key is new, instantiate a new node `new Node(key, value)`, register it in `cache`, and invoke `insert(node)`.

- Step 6: Eviction Handling on Overflow — After adding a new node, if `cache.size > capacity`, evict the least recently used element: the node directly following `left` (`const lru = left.next`). Call `remove(lru)`, delete `lru.key` from `cache`, and finalize the eviction.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(1) strictly for both `get` and `put` operations, as hash map reads/writes and doubly linked list pointer updates all execute in constant time. Space Complexity: O(C) auxiliary space, where C is the maximum capacity of the cache, storing at most C nodes in both the hash map and the linked list.
pseudoCode:
CLASS LRUCache:
    CONSTRUCTOR(capacity):
        cap = capacity, cache = HASH_MAP(), left = Node(0,0), right = Node(0,0)
        left.next = right; right.prev = left
    FUNCTION get(key):
        IF key IN cache THEN REMOVE(cache[key]); INSERT(cache[key]); RETURN cache[key].val
        RETURN -1
    FUNCTION put(key, value):
        IF key IN cache THEN REMOVE(cache[key])
        cache[key] = NEW Node(key, value); INSERT(cache[key])
        IF LENGTH(cache) > cap THEN:
            lru = left.next; REMOVE(lru); DELETE cache[lru.key]
END CLASS

Lines 9-10: put(1, 10) -> Allocate Node(1, 10) at address 0x1A. Insert right before RIGHT sentinel.
Lines 9-10: put(2, 20) -> Allocate Node(2, 20) at address 0x2A. Insert at MRU position. List: [1, 2].
Lines 9-10: put(3, 30) -> Allocate Node(3, 30) at address 0x3A. Cache is now full (3/3). List: [1 (LRU), 2, 3 (MRU)].
Line 6: get(2) -> Key 2 found in cache. Detach Node(2, 20) from current position in DLL.
Line 6: Re-insert Node(2, 20) at MRU position. List is now [1 (LRU), 3, 2 (MRU)]. Returns 20.
Line 12: put(4, 40) -> Current size (3) == capacity (3). Evict LRU node: left.next is Node(1, 10).
Line 12: Remove Node(1, 10) from DLL and delete key 1 from cache map.
Line 10: Insert Node(4, 40) at MRU position. List: [3 (LRU), 2, 4 (MRU)].
Line 7: get(1) -> Key 1 is not in cache (evicted previously). Returns -1 (Cache Miss).
Line 6: get(3) -> Key 3 found in cache. Promote Node(3, 30) from LRU to MRU position. List: [2 (LRU), 4, 3 (MRU)]. Returns 30.
Line 12: put(5, 50) -> Cache full (3/3). Evict LRU node: left.next is Node(2, 20). Remove key 2.
Line 10: Insert Node(5, 50) at MRU position. Final list order: [4 (LRU), 3, 5 (MRU)]. Operations completed.
